title: Solid Effects + Async Short Tour
intent: Explain the split effect path from public API through async scheduling.

steps.title: Concept: compute before apply
steps.body:
# Solid 2.0: Split Effects

The old single callback mixed dependency discovery with side effects. Solid 2.0 separates `compute` from `apply` so the runtime can discover dependencies and async readiness before user effects run.

steps.title: RFC rationale
steps.body: The RFC frames split effects as part of a broader reactivity model: stricter writes, top-level read warnings, batching, async, and boundaries.

anchors.note: Compute records dependencies; effect runs after all compute phases in the batch.

steps.title: effect() creates a lazy computed
steps.body: Internally, an effect is represented as a computed node plus owner/effect-specific fields.

anchors.note: effect() wraps the compute half in computed(..., { lazy: true }).
runEffect is the apply half that executes the side effect with the computed value.

steps.title: handleAsync detects pending work
steps.body: Async values produced during compute are converted into suspension and later resumption.

anchors.note: handleAsync detects Promise-like values or AsyncIterables.
Unresolved promises initialize a transition and throw NotReadyError from the compute path.
